title: Reinforcement Learning-Driven Window Selection for Enhanced Window-Based Rip-up and Reroute in Chip Detailed Routing
problem: Window-based rip-up and reroute in detailed routing is the most runtime-intensive step due to inefficient window selection that targets violations uniformly, wasting effort on low-congestion areas while missing high-congestion routing hotspots.
motivation: Advanced technology nodes impose complex design rules and high pin density, making violation-free layout closure extremely challenging, and rip-up-reroute dominates detailed routing runtime.
method: This approach uses reinforcement learning (AI that learns through trial and error) to intelligently choose which sections of the chip to repair and how large each section should be, instead of treating all areas equally. It positions sections based on where design rule violations (places where routing breaks manufacturing rules) occur, focusing effort on high-congestion areas. The AI learns which window placements eliminate the most violations most efficiently, achieving routing without any violations while maintaining competitive wire length and via count.
key_novelty: This is the first use of reinforcement learning to automatically adjust repair-section size and position based on where design rule violations occur, eliminating all violations while improving wire length and via count.
contributions: Dynamic window generation strategy adjusting size/position based on DRV distribution.
RL-based predictive window selection minimizing design rule violations.
Outperforms TritonRoute with DRV-free solution, 0.07% wirelength improvement, 2.42% via reduction.

metrics.other: DRV-free solution, 0.07% wirelength improvement, 2.42% via reduction, same average runtime as TritonRoute

primary_theme: RL-driven window selection for detailed routing optimization
